rv.q: Thomas Ostermeier's legendary Ibsen production is surreal, provocative and very funny.
A blackboard becomes whitewashed as information is suppressed; Bowie’s Changes frequently stammers in the background.
This latest project is a staging of Ibsen’s An Enemy of the People, as rethought by the German director Thomas Ostermeier.

This achingly – crudely – right-on pair are, of course, in a band, which results in much moody musical noodling between scenes. The set’s chalkboard walls are covered with graffiti, including the gnomic statement: “If you happen to run into the Buddha on the street, kill him.

cn.t: Ostermeier's provocative, anarchic Ibsen adaptation divides critics: some hail its surreal, rock 'n' roll energy and humor, while others find it heavy-handed and surprisingly toothless despite its bold approach.
